title: Question for the `GetUnitSubgraphs` function
body:
In `band/model_analyzer.cc`, I have a question for this code block.
https://github.com/mrsnu/band/blob/236378ef119d8b744b39932ea7b8a3481e0c337b/band/model_analyzer.cc#L354-L362

As the `unsupported_ops` and `op_sets_to_ignore` maps are defined with worker_id, not device id, I think using `tmp_worker_id` corresponding with `device_flag` is not correct.
Suppose,
Worker 0: CPU with CPUMaskFlag::kBig.
Worker 1: CPU with CPUMaskFlag::kLittle,
Worker 2: GPU with CPUMaskFlag::kAll
case.
In that manner, we should find the corresponding unsupported ops' information using `worker_id`, not `device_flag`.

My suggestion is changing the code into

```
if (unsupported_ops.find(worker_id) == unsupported_ops.end() ||
            unsupported_ops.at(worker_id).find(op_index) ==
                unsupported_ops.at(worker_id).end()) {
          if (op_sets_to_ignore[worker_id].find(op_index) ==
              op_sets_to_ignore[worker_id].end()) {
            op_support_table[op_index] |= 1 << worker_id;
          }
        }
```

Could you suggest any ideas?

title: [Platform support] Tensorflow Lite Hexagon Delegate
body:
Currently, Tensorflow Lite requires the end user to add shared libraries to use Hexagon delegate, such as `libhexagon_interface.so` (interface from TensorFlow side - integrated in `org.tensorflow:tensorflow-lite-hexagon` aar) and `libhexagon_nn_skel*.so` (Qualcomm nnlib). 
We want to automate this process with our Java aar and benchmark execution process.

### Problem

The signature for the provided libraries is generated using the `elfsigner` from a Hexagon SDK, allowing for development on test devices. However, it is important to note that execution on production devices, such as OEM devices like Pico 4, requires appropriate credentials from system integrators.

Reference
- https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/issues/49247
- https://developer.qualcomm.com/forum/qdn-forums/software/hexagon-dsp-sdk/toolsinstallation/33337

### Current solution

Simply push and load `libhexagon_nn_skel*.so` to public directories, such as `/data/local/tmp` 

### Possible direction to investigate

See if we can sign these libraries on our own (using Hexagon SDK https://developer.qualcomm.com/software/hexagon-dsp-sdk/tools that requires company registration).

The current implementation has two hierarchy schedulers.
- schedulers[0]: for non-SLO jobs.

title: [Bug] `NeedProfile` vs. `HasSLO`
body:
The current scheduler implementation specifies the profiling requirement by `NeedProfile()` returning `true` or `false`.
Also, when `Engine.Init()`, `NeedProfile()`s for all schedulers are invoked and if there is no scheduler requiring profiling, `latency_estimator_` is not initialized.

However, when a job has a target SLO, a planner retrieves an expected latency from a job and checks if the remaining time is sufficient to consume the job.

Therefore, if the configuration of an engine is set to have a scheduler not requiring profiling and an SLO-specified job is requested, `Engine.GetExpected` will return a default value (0) and the SLO checking logic will not be correct.

I think the engine should always track the latency of every execution, as SLO-specified jobs can always be requested unless checking SLO incurs significant overhead.

title: `Buffer` and Preprocessing library for vision tasks
body:
This partially resolves #275.

### Design goal
* Ultimately, most users do not directly handle the `tensor` object. -> Introduce an arbitrary external memory wrapper (`Buffer`) that is interchangeable with a tensor. Once the post-processing is done, users directly send a request with external data, and `Engine` handles the rest with a pre-registered  `PreProcessor` and `PostProcessor`.

* Bring pre/post-processing into the engine`s control for better controllability (e.g., embed as an internal op of the graph or run on the designated worker for latency guarantee, ...)

### List of changes
* `Buffer` class that abstracts any data object. Currently supports image types, YUV, and tensor.
* Port libyuv-based image-processing backend from `tensorflow-lite-support` (/band/buffer/libyuv_image_operator)
* `BufferProcessorBuilder` and `ImageProcessor`. The user could build their own preprocessor or postprocessor and use it for personal use (transform from buffer to the input tensor - current version) and register it to the engine to directly feed buffer object for the inference request (TODO).
* C API implementation

### Example usage (from `c_api_test`)

``` c++
...
std::tuple<unsigned char*, int, int> image_buffer =
      LoadRGBImageRaw("band/test/data/cat.jpg");
BandBuffer* buffer = BandBufferCreate();
BandBufferSetFromRawData(buffer, std::get<0>(image_buffer),
                           std::get<1>(image_buffer), std::get<2>(image_buffer),
                           kBandRGB);
BandImageProcessorBuilder* builder = BandImageProcessorBuilderCreate();
BandImageProcessor* processor = BandImageProcessorBuilderBuild(builder);
BandImageProcessorProcess(processor, buffer, input_tensor);

BandEngineRequestSync(engine, model, &input_tensor, &output_tensor);
...
```

title: [Java] Allow non-global/r-value ByteBuffer when constructing model
body:
## Current situation:
When creating a model object, the model file's ByteBuffer mustn't be collected by the GC.
However, this might not be done by users (even the Java example given doesn't do this...), and would thus lead to segmentation fault because the model's ByteBuffer is refered to during inference but is collected by the GC.

## Expected behaviour:
Should be able to allocate a model object safely without having to care about the lifetime of the model's ByteBuffer. Or at the very least, there should be an explicit warning about this.

title: Refactor absl #210
body:
Resolves #210 

# List of changes
1. Now, compilation shows warning as an error to be more strict, which is helpful for targeting multiple compilers, except for some verbose warnings. (See `band_copts`)
2. `cc_library` -> `band_cc_library`
3. `BandStatus` -> `absl::Status`
4. Most structs in `c/common.h` are migrated to `common.h` with `enum` -> `enum class`

# Known Issues
1. All error code is `InternalError` for now as abesil error code scheme targets the network errors, but needed to be changed after we refactor the logging system.
2. Some code, such as checking status for return value, are redundant. Need to change those with macros.
3. Current error messages are not carefully decided.

# Note
1. Warnings from external libraries are suppressed, which means `chrome_tracer`, `tensorflow` and `ruy` we revised should be treated carefully.
2. This naively changes the `BandStatus` into `absl::Status`, so this does not refactor the structure of the code, which should be especially for `Subgraph`s.
3. All tests regarding absl::Status should use `EXPECT_EQ(..., absl::OkStatus())` instead of `EXPECT_TRUE(....ok())` because the latter does not show the error code and message.

title: Worker thread affinity propagation to CPU backend
body:
This PR resolves #238, and re-implementation of https://github.com/mrsnu/band/pull/66 on top of the current master.

title: [Core] Intermediate tensor pool
body:
Currently, the intermediate tensor does not have an additional container in the middle of the `Job` execution and has the potential to be overwritten by other `Job`.

The parallel execution of a certain model with three units (e.g., 0 - 1 - 2) with the below sequence shows the exact problem.
[DSP, Job 0 , Unit 0-1] - [DSP, Job 1, Unit 0-1] < Intermediate tensor of `Job 0, Unit 0-1` overwritten by the `Job 1` > - [CPU, Job 0, Unit 2] - [CPU, Job1, Unit 2].

Luckily, we couldn't find a single instance of the above due to the latency-centric / FIFO-based execution scheme, so we left this as future work.

### Expected change
* Detect any potential overwrite (see if previous `Job` took intermediate tensor?)
* Move to a safe place (e.g., designated memory pool for the intermediate tensor #191)

### Problem
Current core components (e.g., `Engine`, `Planner`, and `Worker`) directly copy `Job` instances without explicit life-cycle control.

### Expected changes

title: [ModelAnalyzer] `model_executor->GetOutputs(key)` is not included in `all_outputs`
body:
`c_api_test` is not passed due to the output tensor mismatch caused by XNNPACK delegation.

https://github.com/mrsnu/band/blob/6fff9bfd813c15b28df252f334589648efcb5672/band/engine.cc#L135-L138

I have not found the reason, but `model_executor->GetOutputs` is not included in the `all_outputs`.
It seems `interpreter.outputs` is not updated after replacing the nodes (in add.bin, two AddOps) into the XNNPackDelegateOp for some reason. I am trying to find out why this happens.

## Current status
`all_outputs` retrieves the all output tensors of nodes in `execution_plan`
In `execution_plan`, one node XNNPackDelegationOp exists (because all nodes are supported by XNNPACK), which outputs the tensor indexed by 2.
However, `model_executor->GetOutputs(key)`, which calls `GetInterpreter(key)->outputs()`, returns the tensor indexed by 0.

title: Subgraph support part 1 (Partition)
body:
This PR introduces a bunch of changes for subgraph support of the system.
This PR focuses on a unit subgraph-based partitioning & merging from (#151 #149).
The remaining half will be the system support to schedule/execute subgraphs with proper intermediate tensor communication for correctness.
I would appreciate any comment if you have any :) @JeonChangMin @widiba03304 @juimdpp 

### List of changes
1. Add `ModelAnalyzer` that partitions the given model based on a configuration (corresponds to backend-agnostic logics from old `InterpreterBuilder`.
   - Create `ModelSpec` during partitioning to minimize the statefulness
   - Provide subgraph definitions based on a given partitioning mode
2. Add not implemented `LSF` scheduler to enable partitioning on a planner side
3. Introduce minimal changes in Tensorflow Lite `interpreter_builder` to support the generation of subgraphs for given ops
4. Refactor `SubgraphKey` to have unit indices instead of operators for better explainability
   - I plan to let `Engine` have mapping btwn unit subgraphs to operator indices for ease of scheduling
5. Refactor `Interpreter` to have an explicit target model and worker to avoid misuse
6. Refactor `FallbackPerDevice` to `FallbackPerWorker` 
    - Generate fallback subgraphs to all CPU workers 
7. Silence `INFO` logs from  Tensorflow Lite Delegates to avoid spammy messages on our side
